about.title: Pismo Beach Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone you love changes the shape of every ordinary day, and Pismo Beach is a small enough town — roughly 8,162 residents — that a single death is felt well beyond one household. Public collision records for 2025 show 58 injury crashes in the city and 73 people hurt, with no traffic deaths logged that year. That is welcome news, but wrongful death claims here arise from more than the roadway: a fall at a rental property, a medical error, a boating or workplace incident. When a death is traced to someone else's carelessness, California law gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a civil claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible after them. The window is generally two years from the date of death, and shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We listen, then connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Pismo Beach Families Start With LawProactive

items.title: We sort out who has standing first
items.desc: California limits who may file a wrongful death claim, beginning with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with will confirm where your family fits before anything else.

items.title: We respect a clock that does not pause for grief
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the deadline is shorter when a city, county or state agency is involved. Reaching out early keeps every option open.

items.title: The full loss is counted, not just the receipts
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the love, companionship and guidance that cannot be replaced. An independent attorney works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The crash happened on US-101 through Pismo Beach. Does it matter that the highway belongs to the state?
items.answer: It can matter a great deal. When a claim involves a government entity such as Caltrans, the City of Pismo Beach or San Luis Obispo County, California requires a formal claim on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. That is one reason families along the 101 corridor benefit from speaking with an attorney soon after a loss, even before all the facts are in.

items.question: There is a criminal case against the driver. Do we have to wait for it to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves separately from any criminal prosecution. The two can run at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. Your attorney can explain how evidence from the criminal case may still be useful.

items.question: My father was not married and I am his adult child. Can I bring the claim?
items.answer: Under California law, children stand alongside a surviving spouse or domestic partner in the first group entitled to file. If there is no spouse or partner, the children may proceed on their own. Other dependents and heirs may qualify depending on the family's circumstances, which is exactly the kind of question the attorney will walk through with you.
